# /unit-test

Turn a path, a module, or a **coverage target** into authored-and-run unit tests across the EQOne frontend (`eq-nexus-ui` shell, child MFEs `eq-one-saye-mfe` / `eq-one-sip-mfe` / `eq-one-shares-mfe`, `eq-one-shared`) and the `ExperienceAPI` BFF (`src/domains/<name>/`). `@scanner` finds the untested/under-covered code, `@tester` authors the unit tests (Vitest/Jest on the FE, xUnit/NUnit on the BFF), the suites are run and coverage measured against the target, and `@critic` gates the result — all under the haiku-first model ladder, the cache, and the run budget.

This command is the **main thread**: only it launches subagents by delegating via your `agents` list. **Subagents never launch further subagents.** The whole run is fronted and budgeted by `@supervisor`, gated by `@critic`, with `@decision` resolving any ambiguity (which behaviour a test should pin, whether a module is genuinely untestable as-is, what counts toward the coverage target) with a logged, defensible rationale.

Target under test: **$ARGUMENTS** — a file/dir path, a module/MFE/BFF-domain name, or a coverage target (e.g. `--coverage=85`). Any combination is accepted; a bare path with no number defaults the target to the project's configured coverage threshold.

## Operating model (always on)

- **Console.** Every stage emits the standardised three-part console via the `console-render` skill (see `console/CONSOLE-UX.md`): an **Intro card** at the start, **one block per stage** below, and a **Summary** at the end. Never print ad-hoc output — route it through `console-render`.
- **Budget.** `@supervisor` plans the stages and allocates the tool-call/token budget per `budget-policy`. The `budget-check` skill is tallied after every stage; if a stage would breach the ceiling, `@supervisor` narrows the remaining modules (or trims the coverage target) and makes the go/no-go call before continuing rather than blowing the budget.
- **Model ladder.** Each agent runs at its default tier (`model-routing-policy`) — `@scanner` and `@tester` are **haiku-first** (mechanical scan + rule-based test authoring is the ideal Haiku workload). Escalate exactly ONE rung (`haiku → sonnet`) only on low self-eval confidence (<0.7) or two consecutive `@critic` FAILs; escalation is logged and budgeted, never auto-downgraded.
- **Cache.** The read-only `@scanner` coverage/dead-code scan is served through `cache-lookup` (keyed `skill_id, version, input_hash`, per `cache-policy`) so re-running `/unit-test` on the same tree never re-pays for the same scan. **NEVER cache test writes, test runs, coverage runs, `@critic` verdicts, self-eval, or LLM completions** — those are write/execute side-effecting and non-deterministic; always run fresh.
- **DNA pre-check.** Test authoring is a build step, so `@tester` runs `dna-precheck` before writing — reuse > extend > create over existing fixtures, factories, and test utilities (common test helpers belong in `eq-one-shared` via `@shared-curator` + `move-to-shared`); no duplicated fixtures, no new test framework, no new runtime dependency.
- **Safety/paths.** Honour `safety-rails` (no secrets or PII in fixtures or logs; stub/fake data only) and `path-policy` (`@tester` touches only co-located test files — `*.test.ts(x)`, `*.spec.ts(x)`, `*Tests.cs`; **never** edits production source to force a green test).

## Staged flow

### Stage 0 — Plan & budget (Intro card) — `@supervisor`
`@supervisor` parses `$ARGUMENTS` (path vs module vs coverage target), plans the stages, allocates the tool-call/token budget per `budget-policy`, and emits the **Intro card** via `console-render` (target under test, repos/modules in scope, coverage target, budget ceiling). It seeds the `TodoWrite` ledger (one item per module to be tested) and **opens the agent-memory runtime** under `.eq-sparks/agent-memory/<run-id>/` (`metadata.json`, `scratchpad.md`, idempotent `ledger.jsonl`, `handoff/`) per the `memory-schema` runtime layout, so the run is auditable and `/resume`-able.

### Stage 1 — Find untested code (`@scanner`, read-only, cached)
Launch `@scanner` (haiku) to map the target to a concrete set of source units and find what is untested or under-covered: parse the existing coverage report if one exists, otherwise enumerate source units (functions/components/handlers) and cross-reference co-located `*.test.ts(x)` / `*.spec.ts(x)` / `*Tests.cs` files to find gaps and dead/uncovered branches. Read-only, mechanical pattern work — served through `cache-lookup` on the tree hash. `@scanner` reports **findings only** (it does not judge or author); if a unit's intended behaviour is ambiguous or it looks untestable as-written, it flags it rather than guessing. Emits a **stage block** of the gap map (per module: units, current coverage, missing cases), then routes a structured **handoff envelope** (`handoff` skill, `methodology/handoff-protocol.md`) carrying the per-module gap map to Stage 2. If any unit's expected behaviour is undecided, `@supervisor` launches `@decision` (opus) to make the call and log the rationale before authoring begins.

### Stage 2 — Author tests (`@tester`, PARALLEL per module)
Launch one `@tester` (haiku) **per independent module** — the gap map partitions the work by MFE / `eq-one-shared` / BFF domain, and those partitions touch disjoint co-located test files, so they run **concurrently** (see **Parallelisation**). Each `@tester` reads the inbound envelope addressed to it, runs its **autoresearch loop** (`methodology/autoresearch-loop.md`) with **`dna-precheck` first** (reuse existing fixtures/factories/test utils; no duplicate helpers, no new framework or runtime dep) and **`self-evaluate` last**, authors/extends the co-located unit tests for its module (happy path plus the key edge/error cases per the gap map), and emits a `handoff` envelope back. A `@tester` that hits ambiguous test logic stops with `BLOCKED:ambiguous-test-logic` and routes back through `@supervisor` to `@decision`. No production source is edited.

### Stage 3 — Run suites + measure coverage (`@tester`, fresh — never cached)
Run the authored suites scoped to the affected files/suites (Vitest/Jest with `--coverage` on the FE; `dotnet test` with a coverage collector on the BFF) and measure coverage against the target. **Always executes fresh** — test/coverage runs are never cached or fabricated (`cache-policy`). `@tester` captures PASS/FAIL counts, the verbatim failure trace for any failure, and the per-module + aggregate coverage numbers. If a test reveals a real production defect (not a test bug), `@tester` stops with `BLOCKED:source-change-required` and routes back through `@supervisor` to `@codegen` (FE) / `@db` (BFF data-access) — this orchestrator authors tests, it does not fix product code. Emits a **stage block** with PASS/FAIL and coverage delta vs target.

### Stage 4 — Critic gate (BARRIER) — `@critic`
**Barrier.** Stage 2/3's parallel `@tester` runs must **all complete** and their handoff envelopes be on disk before `@critic` is launched — `@critic` gates the *aggregated* result, never a partial one. `@critic` (opus) adversarially reviews the authored tests + run results + coverage against EQ standards and the coverage target, and returns strict **PASS / FAIL** with required changes (e.g. missing edge case, assertion that does not actually pin behaviour, coverage target not met, a fixture that smuggles in real data). A **FAIL BLOCKS** the run and routes the envelope **back to the offending `@tester`** (Stage 2) — re-run that module, escalate one tier (`haiku → sonnet`) only after two consecutive FAILs (logged + budgeted), then re-run + re-gate. Only a PASS advances. Emits the gate block.

### Stage 5 — Summary — `@supervisor`
`@supervisor` makes the final go/no-go, runs `budget-check` one final time, and **aggregates every** `handoff/*.json` envelope under the run's `handoff/` in `seq` order. It emits the **Summary** via `console-render`: tests authored per module, final PASS/FAIL counts, per-module + aggregate coverage vs the target (met / shortfall), any `BLOCKED:` hand-backs (defects routed to `@codegen`/`@db`, ambiguities to `@decision`), tier escalations taken, cache hit-rate, and budget spent vs ceiling. The `agent-memory` ledger is closed for a clean `/resume`.

## Handoff & memory

Stages **compose** by passing a structured **handoff envelope**, never free text — written and read via the `handoff` skill per `methodology/handoff-protocol.md` and stored at `.eq-sparks/agent-memory/<run-id>/handoff/<seq>-<from>-to-<to>.json`.
- **Routing.** The orchestrator (the main thread) is the router: `@scanner`'s gap map → each `@tester` (the per-module envelopes fan the work out), each `@tester`'s authored tests + run/coverage results → `@critic`, `@critic`'s PASS/FAIL → `@supervisor`. On a `@critic` FAIL the envelope routes **back** to the producing `@tester` (Stage 2) with the required changes in `open_items`. `BLOCKED:` hand-backs (defect → `@codegen`/`@db`, ambiguity → `@decision`) route through `@supervisor`.
- **Memory runtime.** At Stage 0 `@supervisor` opens the per-run agent-memory directory (`.eq-sparks/agent-memory/<run-id>/`: `metadata.json`, `scratchpad.md`, idempotent `ledger.jsonl`, `handoff/<seq>-<from>-to-<to>.json`) per the `memory-schema` runtime layout, instantiated from `shared/memory/templates/`, and updates the ledger as each module moves `pending` → `done`/`blocked`.
- **Loop + self-eval.** `@tester` runs the **autoresearch loop** (`methodology/autoresearch-loop.md`) with `dna-precheck` at entry and the diff-based `self-evaluate` as the mandatory LAST step (it is a `writesDiff` agent) before emitting its envelope; `@scanner` is read-only and self-assesses; `@critic`/`@supervisor` gate/assess.
- **Aggregation.** At Stage 5 `@supervisor` reads **every** `handoff/*.json` in `seq` order and rolls the chain, tests authored, coverage, decisions, escalations, open items, and final budget into the `console-render` Summary — reconstructed from on-disk record, not recollection.

## Parallelisation

- **PARALLEL — Stage 2/3 authoring.** The Stage 1 gap map partitions the work **by module** (MFE / `eq-one-shared` / BFF domain), and those partitions write disjoint co-located test files, so `@supervisor` launches **one `@tester` per module concurrently**. Each authors AND runs its own scoped suite/coverage independently — they share no test files, so there is no write contention.
- **BARRIER — at the `@critic` gate (Stage 4).** The parallel `@tester` runs **fan back in** here: all per-module envelopes must be on disk before `@critic` is launched, because `@critic` gates the aggregated tests + coverage as one verdict. No `@tester` proceeds past Stage 3 until the barrier is reached.
- **SEQUENTIAL — everything else.** Stage 0 (plan) → Stage 1 (scan) → [parallel Stage 2/3] → Stage 4 (gate) → Stage 5 (summary) run in order. A `@critic` FAIL re-runs only the offending module's `@tester`, then re-hits the barrier and re-gates. `@decision` (ambiguity) and any `BLOCKED:` defect hand-backs are resolved before the affected module's authoring continues.

## Steps

1. Launch `@supervisor` (`Agent`) to parse `$ARGUMENTS` (path / module / coverage target), plan the stages + budget from `budget-policy`, seed the `TodoWrite` ledger, open the `agent-memory` runtime (`memory-schema`), and emit the **Intro card** via `console-render`.
2. Launch `@scanner` (`Agent`, haiku, via `cache-lookup`) to map the target to source units and produce the per-module **gap map** (untested/under-covered units + missing cases). If a unit's expected behaviour is ambiguous, launch `@decision` (`Agent`) for a logged call before authoring.
3. Launch **one `@tester` per independent module IN PARALLEL** (`Agent`, haiku) — each reads its inbound `handoff` envelope, runs `dna-precheck` first, authors/extends the co-located unit tests, then runs the scoped suite **with coverage** (fresh, never cached), and runs `self-evaluate` last before emitting its envelope. No production source edits.
4. **Barrier:** wait for **all** parallel `@tester` envelopes, then launch `@critic` (`Agent`, opus) for the strict PASS/FAIL gate over the aggregated tests + coverage vs target.
5. On FAIL: route back to the offending `@tester` (re-run only that module, escalate one tier after two consecutive FAILs per `model-routing-policy`), re-run + re-measure, re-hit the barrier, and re-gate. On a `BLOCKED:source-change-required` defect, hand back to `@codegen`/`@db` via `@supervisor`. On PASS: continue.
6. Launch `@supervisor` (`Agent`) for the final go/no-go; run `budget-check`; aggregate every `handoff/*.json` envelope in `seq` order and emit the **Summary** via `console-render` (tests authored, PASS/FAIL, coverage vs target, escalations, open items, cache hit-rate, budget). Close the `agent-memory` ledger.

## Usage

```
/unit-test packages/eq-one-saye-mfe/src/components/ContributionsPanel.tsx
```
Author and run unit tests for a single file: `@scanner` finds its untested branches, one `@tester` authors Vitest tests against the SAYE MFE conventions, runs them with coverage, and `@critic` gates the result.

```
/unit-test eq-one-shared --coverage=90
```
Drive a whole module to a 90% coverage target: `@scanner` maps the gap, `@tester` authors tests for the uncovered units (parallel per sub-area), runs coverage, and the run loops on `@critic` FAIL until the target is met or `@supervisor` calls budget stop.

```
/unit-test ExperienceAPI/src/domains/sip
```
BFF domain: `@scanner` finds untested handlers/services in the `sip` domain, `@tester` authors xUnit/NUnit tests, runs `dotnet test` with a coverage collector, and `@critic` gates. A real defect surfaced by a test is handed back to `@db`/`@codegen`, not fixed here.

```
/unit-test eq-one-saye-mfe eq-one-sip-mfe --coverage=85
```
Two independent modules to an 85% target: `@scanner` produces a gap map per MFE, `@supervisor` launches **one `@tester` per MFE in parallel**, both fan back in at the `@critic` barrier for a single aggregated PASS/FAIL.

## Resume & checkpoint (interruption-safe)

This orchestrator is resumable after any interruption (IDE closed, crash, cancel). At **Stage 0** the orchestrator writes `.eq-sparks/agent-memory/<run-id>/metadata.json` with `orchestrator: "unit-test"` and the ordered `stages` list, and seeds `ledger.jsonl` with each stage `pending`. After **every** stage passes its gate, the orchestrator — the main thread, which holds `Write`; `@supervisor` is read-only and only specifies *what* to record — **appends a `done` line** to `ledger.jsonl` with that stage's `task_id` + `content_hash` (per [dedup-policy](../shared/guardrails/dedup-policy.md) / [memory-schema](../shared/memory/memory-schema.md)). The ledger is written **incrementally after every stage, not only at the end**, so finished stages survive an interruption. PBI/Figma context is read from the no-TTL **story cache** `.eq-sparks/cache/story-cache/<pbi>.json` and is **never re-fetched**. If interrupted, **`/resume`** reads `metadata.json`, re-enters *this* orchestrator at the first `pending` stage, and skips work already marked `done`.
